$comment: Curated Wikimedia Commons photos, one per week (ADR-003). Selection is a human/curation judgement and lives here; `npm run survey-commons` shortlists the candidates; `npm run commons-images` does the mechanical part — fetch metadata, check the licence against ALLOWED_COMMONS_LICENSES, download, resize, and write the `image` object into data/comparisons.json. To change a photo, change the `commonsTitle` here and re-run. `authorOverride` exists only to trim obvious import noise from the Commons Artist field (a Flickr geographic suffix, say); it must still name the same author, and the script refuses one that does not.

picks.altText: Poppy seeds magnified far past life size, each one kidney-shaped and covered in a fine honeycomb pattern.
picks.why: A USGS Bee Inventory macro, public domain. The extreme magnification suits week 2, where the whole point is how small a poppy seed is; the honeycomb seed coat is only visible at this scale.
picks.authorOverride: USGS Bee Inventory and Monitoring Lab
picks.authorOverrideWhy: Commons carries the Flickr-import form, 'USGS Bee Inventory and Monitoring Lab from Beltsville, Maryland, USA', which wraps the credit line onto two lines. Same author, geographic suffix dropped.

picks.altText: A round dish filled with nyjer seeds, thin black slivers packed tightly together.
picks.why: Clean overhead shot with individual seeds legible. Same photographer and framing as the week 5 millet, so the two cards sit together well.

picks.altText: A round dish of white proso millet, small pale round grains with a faint sheen.
picks.why: Matches the week 4 nyjer shot in framing and lighting.

picks.altText: Black oil sunflower seeds close up, teardrop-shaped shells with fine pale stripes.
picks.why: Sharp macro of black oil sunflower specifically, which is what the week 6 fact is about.

picks.commonsTitle: File:Hirundo rustica gutturalis nest and 4 eggs.jpg
picks.altText: Four small speckled pink eggs in a barn swallow's nest of dried grass and mud, lined with white feathers.
picks.why: A real clutch, close enough that the speckling reads, and the eggs sit near the middle of a landscape frame — which is what the 150px strip crop needs. Chosen from the shortlist over the museum specimen plate.

picks.altText: Three turquoise-blue American Robin eggs resting in a deep nest of dried grass and mud.
picks.why: The colour is the whole point of a robin's egg and it is unmistakable here. Used on fourteen Wikimedia pages. The eggs sit low in the frame, so check the crop.

picks.altText: Three heavily blotched Black Tern eggs on a floating nest of reeds and stems at the surface of a marsh.
picks.why: Shows the floating marsh nest the week's fact is about, not just the eggs. Public domain, USFWS. Foreground leaves intrude at the edges.

picks.altText: A Ruby-throated Hummingbird hovering at a scarlet beebalm flower, wings blurred, its green back catching the light.
picks.why: Author's second-pass pick (14B). Quality and Valued image, used in the species' Wikipedia article. The bird is large in the frame, which the first pick was not. It is a female, so there is no ruby throat.

picks.altText: A Ruby-crowned Kinglet perched on a thin bare twig, its olive back and white wing bar lit from the side.
picks.why: Author's pick (15A). Featured Picture, and the one Wikipedia uses. Bird centred, background clean.

picks.altText: A Black-capped Chickadee perched on a branch stub, its black cap and bib sharp against a soft green background.
picks.why: Author's second-pass pick (16D). One bird, dead centre, clean background — the first pick had a goldfinch in it as well, on a card about one bird's size.

picks.altText: A Carolina Wren on a bare branch with its tail cocked upward, the white stripe over its eye clearly marked.
picks.why: Author's pick (17A). Quality Image, used in the species' Wikipedia article. Large, centred, unambiguous.

picks.altText: A Tufted Titmouse standing on a pale branch against a plain background, its grey crest raised.
picks.why: Author's pick (18A). Featured Picture, used in the species' Wikipedia article. The plain background is ideal for the strip.

picks.altText: A Cedar Waxwing perched among serviceberry leaves and green berries, its crest smooth and its black mask clear.
picks.why: Author's second-pass pick (19C). One bird rather than three, and the berries are the subject of the week's fact.

picks.altText: An Eastern Bluebird perched on a thin branch among new spring leaves, its blue back and rust-coloured breast turned to the camera.
picks.why: Author's pick (20F), taken under protest — the whole week 20 shortlist is weak. See the note in the survey; nothing in the Sialia sialis pool carried a Featured or Quality badge.

picks.commonsTitle: File:American kestrel (Falco sparverius sparveroides) female white morph.JPG
picks.altText: A pale female American Kestrel perched on a bare twig, finely streaked below, with the dark facial markings of the species.
picks.why: Author's pick (21C). Quality and Valued image — but it is the Cuban subspecies in its white morph, which looks little like the kestrel a North American reader pictures. Flagged for reconsideration.

picks.altText: A Blue Jay in sharp profile on a branch, its barred blue wing, white face and black neck ring all clear.
picks.why: Author's pick (22E). A western subspecies but it reads as the textbook Blue Jay, and the wide 2:1 frame suits the strip crop better than the taller candidates.

notSourced.reason: No suitable Commons photo found. Searches for poultry grit, pigeon grit, gizzard grit and granite grit return only scanned pages from pre-1920 poultry manuals; searches for coarse sand return beach and sandstone geology, which does not read as grit a bird would swallow. This is moot until the comparison itself is settled: week 3 is still `proposed: true`, and the P1 fact-check found its only citation (the Wikipedia Gizzard article) never mentions grouse, doves or roadsides. Decide the comparison first.

Commons has no House Wren egg photograph. There is no 'Troglodytes aedon eggs' category at all — checked directly, not inferred from the shortlist — and the species category's egg/nest shortlist is six frames of an adult wren at a nest box, one of them a Featured Picture. A bird on a nest box is not an egg. Author's call, 2026-09-13: leave it as 'Photo coming'.

One shippable candidate in the whole category, and it is a thrush on a nest shot through heavy foliage — unreadable once cropped to the 150px strip. No 'Hylocichla mustelina eggs' category exists. Author's call, 2026-09-13: leave it as 'Photo coming'.

No 'Ardea herodias eggs' category exists. The nest candidates are all rookery shots taken from below, backlit against bright sky, with the nests reading as silhouettes and no eggs visible. Author's call, 2026-09-13: leave it as 'Photo coming'.

Unlike weeks 7, 9 and 12 this one has shippable candidates — a Muséum de Toulouse specimen plate and several nest-with-clutch frames — but the author reviewed them on 2026-09-13 and none shows the egg alone in a natural context: the specimen is on a black studio background, and in the nest shots the eggs are incidental to an adult bird. Needs a source other than Commons, not a better Commons search. Leave it as 'Photo coming'.
